# Incident Report: PCAP Forensic Analysis — 2024-08-15

## Victim Host
| Field | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** | Conversation stats, DHCP, ARP |
| MAC | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** | ARP (`10.8.15.133 -> 00:1c:bf:03:54:82`), matches DHCP client MAC |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** | DHCP option 12 hostname; NBNS `<00>`/`<20>` registration; Kerberos AS-REQ CName `DESKTOP-H8ALZBV$` |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** | Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS CNameString `plucero` from 10.8.15.133 |
| AD domain | lafontainebleu.org (DC WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS) | DNS SRV lookups, Kerberos/LDAP/DRSUAPI traffic |

## Malware Family
**GootLoader**, delivered via a fake FedEx-invoice SEO-poisoning/phishing page, followed by an unidentified secondary payload (DLL) fetched via BITS.

**Attribution: behavioral**, based on the following distinctive traits (no external IDS/AV artifacts were present in the evidence directory to confirm by signature):
- Initial access is a ZIP archive named `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` downloaded from a spoofed FedEx invoice-lookup page (`quote.checkfedexexp.com`).
- The extracted `.js` file is **6.99 MB**, almost entirely junk-padded with scraped, unrelated legitimate text (MPI standard documentation, OECD/IPCC report excerpts, Mozilla/Firefox source-doc URLs) around a small functional JScript payload — the signature "giant obfuscated JS invoice dropper padded with scraped web content" technique associated with GootLoader.
- The script embeds a callback URL to `business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?...`, matching the second domain queried by the host minutes after the JS download (classic GootLoader stage-1 check-in/telemetry beacon).
- Minutes later the host used **Microsoft BITS** (`User-Agent: Microsoft BITS/7.8`) to pull a **PE32+ x86-64 DLL** from `72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`, consistent with GootLoader's BITSAdmin-based stage-2 delivery pattern.
- Immediately after, the host began sustained HTTP beaconing (GET and POST to `/` at the bare IP `72.5.43.29`, no hostname/SNI) with an anachronistic hardcoded User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`, carrying encrypted/binary POST bodies and mostly receiving HTTP 400 responses — a bare-IP HTTP host header and hardcoded stale UA are classic C2 tells, but the specific final-stage family could not be confirmed from traffic alone.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — DLL staging (`GET/HEAD /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`) and ongoing encrypted beaconing (`GET /`, `POST /`), first contact at t+135.9s, continuing beyond t+1900s. No DNS lookup preceded this connection (hardcoded IP).

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159) — delivered the phishing ZIP/JS
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70) — JS-embedded callback domain

**Malicious URLs**
- `https://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — served the ZIP archive containing the GootLoader JS
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — BITS-fetched DLL payload

**Transferred files**
- `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` — GootLoader stage-1 JScript dropper (extracted from the ZIP HTTP response), SHA256 `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c`
- ZIP container delivering that JS, SHA256 `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5`
- `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — PE32+ x86-64 DLL fetched via BITS, SHA256 `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6`

**Benign context (excluded from IOCs)**
- All `*.microsoft.com`, `*.msn.com`, `*.bing.com`, `*.windows.com`, Adobe update checks (`acroipm2.adobe.com`, `armmf.adobe.com`), `msftconnecttest.com`, `scorecardresearch.com`, `nelreports.net` (Norton telemetry) — normal Windows/Edge/Office/AV background traffic.
- `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` file downloads — legitimate Windows Delivery Optimization content.

## Incident Summary
User **plucero** on Windows workstation **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (10.8.15.133, MAC 00:1c:bf:03:54:82), a member of the **lafontainebleu.org** AD domain, visited a spoofed FedEx invoice page at `quote.checkfedexexp.com` and downloaded a ZIP archive containing a heavily junk-padded 6.99 MB JScript file (`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`), consistent with GootLoader's initial-access technique. Minutes later the host used BITS to retrieve a PE32+ DLL from `72.5.43.29`, then began sustained encrypted HTTP beaconing to that same bare IP on port 80 using a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer user-agent, indicating successful second-stage payload execution and active C2 communication at the time the capture ended.
